clue.text: Heavenly food in country retreat

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the country's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Annam is an old name for a country, now central Vietnam

explanation.surface: A divine meal is served at a rural hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun, a country retreat, but it is a verb telling you to turn ANNAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible this was the food sent from heaven to feed the Israelites in the desert.

clue.text: Map with charts being organised for a military review

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, as things being organised are arranged

explanation.surface: A soldier sorts maps and charts for an army inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being organised' rearranges MAP and CHARTS together. 'with' and 'for a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade of troops filing past a saluting officer is a ceremonial inspection.

clue.text: Hospital in pleasant, suitable situation

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, the hospital inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital sits in a pleasant, well-suited spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A role or position that suits someone exactly is their ideal place.

clue.text: Fools going around wrong-doing — criminals

annotationWithheld.why: Fools going around wrong-doing — criminals (9), printed so: ASSES round SIN gives no ASSASSINS and no other parse produces the letters

clue.text: Showing firm backbone, a trainee's colouring

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a chine is an animal's backbone, or a cut of meat including it
taken as written
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner of firm character shows off their dye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' and the possessive 's are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This red dye, made from crushed insects, is used to colour food.

clue.text: None in prison can make money

annotationWithheld.why: None in prison can make money (7): the only parse is O + IN inside CAGE, where 'in' is both the IN piece and the container indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: None in prison can make money

clue.text: Outline, to read before a journey

indicators.note: the reading comes in front of the journey

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: A traveller studies the plan before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to read' is CON, an old verb for studying a text.
explanation.definitionFit: The shape of something drawn as a line around its edge is its profile.

clue.text: Not fitting in a work-out?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
PT is physical training, a work-out

explanation.surface: Someone feels out of place at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is gym exercise at school or in the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsuitable or out of place is inappropriate.

clue.text: "Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and — " (Milton).

definitions.text: Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and

parts.words: Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and
parts.note: a line from Milton's Paradise Regained praising Athens; the missing final word completes the quotation

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Paradise Regained, Book IV; the solver supplies the missing last word, the art of fine speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens was the home of oratory, so the missing word is the gift of fluent, persuasive speech.

clue.text: Having left school, this must be revealed

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Once someone leaves school, a secret will come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'this must be' are link words; to let on is to reveal.
explanation.definitionFit: To divulge a secret is to admit or disclose it, an informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Touching submission indicating a slowdown

parts.note: RE means concerning or touching on, as in business letters
a cession is a yielding or surrender of rights or land

explanation.surface: A moving surrender is a sign that things are winding down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' reads as moving or emotional, but it is RE, meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic downturn is a period when business activity slows and shrinks.

clue.text: A measure in preparation

parts.note: taken as written
a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone takes a measurement while getting things ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that are being made or under way are said to be in progress, on the go.

clue.text: Contemptible people — invariably down-trodden

definitions.meaning: the back parts of shoes, or of feet, are always being trodden down

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: the rear part of footwear is pressed into the ground with every step.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cads and the back of the foot or shoe, which is trodden down with every step.

clue.text: The way serving men get ordered around!

definitions.text: The way serving men get ordered around!

parts.words: The way serving men get ordered around!
parts.note: serving men are soldiers, and the command for them to face the opposite way is what is meant; 'ordered around' reads as bossed about

explanation.surface: Servants are bossed about by their masters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving men' suggests servants, but it means men serving in the army, ordered to turn to face the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: On the parade ground soldiers are given this command to reverse the direction they face.

clue.text: A fifties item altered forever

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties are LL

indicators.note: the letters of the word item are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of 1950s memorabilia has been changed for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges ITEM into TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsurpassed in all history is described this way, like a record that stands for ever.

clue.text: Most, injudicious — in America anyway

definitions.meaning: an American word meaning at any rate

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer means 'most foolish'; as one, it is US for 'at least'.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means least sensible; as one it is US usage for at any rate.

clue.text: Income from flat in a Parisian street

indicators.note: one word is placed inside another, here inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means level or flat

explanation.surface: Someone earns money from letting an apartment in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' reads as an apartment but means level, EVEN. 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A government's or business's earnings are its takings or receipts.

clue.text: Honest woman with many financial obligations

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A woman is deep in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; C for 'many' is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A truthful person is one who habitually tells the truth.

clue.text: Enrol volunteers in' harbour

parts.note: to enter someone is to enrol them
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteers sign up in a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' looks like a port but is the verb, to harbour a thought.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour an idea is to hold or consider it in the mind.

clue.text: Beam as son breaks into a vehicle

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, here the jumbled son inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: the word son is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A ray of light falls as a boy forces his way into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a smile or a ray of light, but it is a crossbar. 'breaks' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container; 'as' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a horizontal crossbar, such as the bar over a door or the beam across a ship's stern.

clue.text: Doing damage to fine porcelain without point

indicators.note: without means outside here, the porcelain wrapping around the point

parts.note: Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty
aim is purpose or point

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a valuable vase for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without point' looks like 'pointless', but here 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the porcelain wraps round the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Injuring or crippling someone is inflicting serious harm on them.

clue.text: The Left capturing a number, would be a forewarning

indicators.note: one piece takes another prisoner inside itself, the number going within the word for left

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Left-wing politicians seizing a seat would be an ominous sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Left' suggests a political party, but it is PORT, the nautical left. 'would be a' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen or sign of something momentous to come is a warning given in advance.

clue.text: Leaf-insect display

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Leaf insects put on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf-insect' is a real creature, but here it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand public procession or show in costume is a spectacle.

clue.text: Reporting in store?

definitions.meaning: telling a story over again, recounting
the trade of selling goods to the public in shops

explanation.walkthrough: Retailing means both re-telling a story and selling in shops; 'in store' reads as waiting in the future.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means recounting news, and also the shopkeeper's trade of selling goods to customers.

clue.text: Sack the fellow in anger

indicators.note: the fellow goes inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile someone is to anger them
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Someone fires a man in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' means plunder, not dismiss; 'anger' is the verb RILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack or plunder a place is to search through it and steal.

clue.text: Some complain terribly and get put down

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Complain loudly and you will be squashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'and get', which are link words; 'put down' alone means bury.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to lay it in the ground.

clue.text: Bound by the accountant firstly

indicators.note: the accountant comes first, ahead of the word for by

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: An accountant is held, first of all, by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like tied, but it is the verb to leap. 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip or leap about playfully is a synonym of jump.

clue.text: Set out for the factory

definitions.meaning: to place in the ground, as seedlings

explanation.walkthrough: 'for the' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to put seedlings in the ground, and also an industrial works.

clue.text: It's so hard now in Clwyd

definitions.meaning: a very hard grey stone, used for striking sparks
a town in north Wales, at the time of the puzzle in the county of Clwyd

explanation.walkthrough: Clwyd was a Welsh county from 1974 to 1996; 'now' places the town in it at the time of printing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a hard quartz stone, proverbially hard, and also the name of a Welsh town and its old county.

clue.text: One loved acquiring a small figure at a Roman retreat!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the smallest figure

indicators.note: the words go backwards, so at a Roman is read from the end

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is found at a Roman villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reverses AT A ROMAN to NAMORATA; 'acquiring' joins it to I.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian word names a woman who is the object of someone's love, a sweetheart.

clue.text: Simple optical aid

parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb, so this is a herb that helps the eyes, not plain spectacles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' reads as basic, but in old herbal lore a simple is a medicinal plant; this one was used to treat the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild plant, Euphrasia, was traditionally used as a remedy for eye complaints.

clue.text: Stuff worn when posing for a portrait?

definitions.text: worn when posing for a portrait?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, it says what you did in your clothes while modelling for a painter

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer in two and it describes posing seated in clothes for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth glossy fabric is a kind of cloth, and stuff is an old word for cloth.
